strengths:
brand-type: - The opening works. The e∞ mark draws in one stroke on Night, a soft light edge reveals the bottle on wet stone, and the "Salt, stone / and golden hour." break sits in open sea, well clear of the bottle (5.5 s). The end card (94.5 s) closes on the same film and scrim, so the film is bookended.
- Colour tokens survive the encode. Linen, Night, Golden hour, Sea slate, Blush and Deep sea all sample within 3 of their hex values. Golden hour is the only warm accent outside the scent worlds. Eyebrows follow one rule: 18 px, 0.14em caps, Ash on light grounds and Dune on dark.
- The left margin at x 120 holds all through the film, including optical corrections: the italic Y and d in 04B are hung so their ink lines up with the eyebrow. Display kerning in Cormorant is clean at 120–168 px, with the Th ligature in "Three", and the è in "Matière" is correct.
- Photography mostly feels like one hour of light: the plaster wall, salt on wet stone, the boat in amber fog, the triptych and the after-dark resin. Pushes stay small and slow.
- Colour (06) is the strongest system slide. The 70/20/6/4 bar works as the picture, and the scent worlds are honestly labelled "from the packshot" or "proposed". The triptych uses the three line tones as text bands with no extra boxes, which is exactly the direction's "hairlines, not boxes".
- The type specimen (07) uses real brand lines. The buttons have radius 0 and no shadow. There are no badges, cursors or effects anywhere.

motion-pacing: - The opening is confident and unhurried. There are 0.25 s of Night, then the e∞ mark draws in one even stroke (0.3–1.4 s) and holds 0.5 s. A light edge then reveals the bottle (1.95–2.9 s), and the headline lands word by word at 3.6–4.5 s, over water that is already moving. Do not speed this up.
- The hero film never stutters. The 30 fps frame blending of the 24 fps loop gives uniform frame-to-frame change (mean abs diff about 0.77 through 4–7 s and 89.5–94.7 s). The loop seams at 5.54 s and 93.84 s measure 0.85–0.88, within the film's normal frame-to-frame variation (similar peaks at 5.33 and 93.63). They are invisible. In scene 02 the water continues on scene 01's clock with no jump.
- The 03→04 light-wipe (33.8–35.0) is the best cut in the film. The Wayne field, chip and watermark are pixel-identical in both scenes, so only the left of the frame changes as the light passes. Keep that match exactly.
- The entrance grammar is consistent across all 11 scenes: 24 px emphasized rise for display words and 16 px standard for small type, an 80 ms word stagger, and fade-only exits. Nothing snaps. Word rises settle without sub-pixel stepping.
- Pushes and scrolls are smooth. Per-frame diffs during the P1–P3 pushes, the boat push and both storefront drifts are even (for example 0.26–0.34 across 27.0–27.6). Phone B's scroll has a clean sine ease-in and ease-out and no judder.
- The close bookends the opening with the same framing, scrim and push. The water keeps breathing under the wordmark to the last frame, and the last frame (94.67) is the end card. It is a beautiful end card.
- Principles 1–3 are revealed by a soft light edge, with the words rising as the light settles. This demonstrates the direction's motion language while presenting it.

finishing-qa: Compliance is clean. No scene loads og-image, house-founder, tale-mercury, finder-time-both or finder-who-either. Every person is seen from behind: I zoomed in on the couple, the eterno man, the fisherman and the Forbidden Apple figure. The captures show no prices, no brackets, no blank announcement bar and no product cards, and there is no Arabic anywhere. Every tale line, house line and site line matches content/tales.ts, content/scents.ts and components/home/Sections.tsx exactly, and the board lines match the direction boards. All text sits inside title-safe.

Colour survives the encode. On every flat field I sampled, the brand hex values in the MP4 are within 1–3 code values: Linen 242/237/230, Night 22/22/19, Golden hour 184/120/42, Deep sea 20/57/76, and all ten world tiles. The 1 px Dune hairlines stay single-pixel and crisp.

The encode is clean in time. There are no one-frame glitches and no keyframe pop at the segment joins (31.57 s, 63.13 s). Hold frames are truly static (diff 0.00). The hero-film loop seam (5.54 s, 11.08 s, 93.84 s) is invisible, and the grain on Night survives with no blocking. Frame 0 is Night with grain, and the last frame (94.667 s) is the full end card: wordmark, hairline and tagline.

Motion that works:
- The mark draws cleanly.
- No push reveals an image edge.
- The P3 light band sweeps with no seam.
- The P4 chip and watermark stay in register through the wipe into scene 04.
- The Wayne photo shows no bars or rounded corners at full push, and line-eterno shows no white border.
- The storefront scroll ranges stay inside their safe css offsets.

Keep all of this while fixing.

client-eye: As the owner, a lot of this feels like my house and I want it kept.

- **Opening (0–7 s).** Near-black, one stroke of light, then my Wayne bottle on wet stone at golden hour with "Salt, stone and golden hour." set in the open sea. It is expensive and calm, and nothing crosses the bottle.
- **Ending (89.5–94.7 s).** The film comes back to the same light and holds the wordmark and "Some things are never meant to fade." as the end card. It is a proper bookend and a strong frame to leave up in the room.
- **Shadow of the Sea (41–45.9 s).** The boat in amber fog, full-bleed with the italic line over the dark water, is the emotional peak. The tale lines are my real lines, typeset beautifully.
- **Three lines triptych (51–54.7 s).** Each person is seen from behind, each photo sits on its tone band, and the names are lowercase. It is instantly clear and it is the loveliest frame after the opening.
- **Honest colour worlds (60–64 s).** The ratio bar makes the discipline tangible, and each world is labelled "from the packshot" or "proposed". I trust an agency that does not pretend proposals are final.
- **Real site pages.** The tales page and the mood tiles (76–82 s) and the two phones (82–89 s) are sharp and legible at full size. The film really does look like the site.
- **Motion that practises what it preaches.** Slow pushes, word rises, soft light reveals, no gimmicks. The film loop seam is invisible.

Keep:
- the opening and closing frames
- the fog-boat beat
- the triptych
- the "proposed" labels
- the unhurried rhythm

findings.problem: Every runtime crossfade and the dip-to-linen use R.ease.standard. That curve is front-loaded (0.20, 0.40, 0.56 after frames 1–3), so a "0.6 s crossfade" is really a ~0.1 s jolt followed by a long ghost tail. The worst case is the dip out of the boat tale: the amber frame flashes to Linen in about 4 frames.
findings.evidence: Encoded-MP4 frame-difference analysis (mean abs diff, 240×135 luma) shows a one-frame spike at the first frame of every runtime transition. Values: 45.933 → 30.0 (dip), 54.733 → 21.1, 69.733 → 24.7, 75.133 → 21.4, 14.433 → 10.7, 64.133 → 9.3. Mid-transition frames sit around 2–6. Strip 45.6–47.4: at 46.00 the boat is already half-washed, and by 46.13 it is almost gone. Strip 69.4–70.6: at 69.80 the charcoal panel is already about 56 % in.
findings.fix: In runtime.js applyIn(), change the crossfade opacity to R.ease.inOut(p), which is the same symmetric curve the light-wipe already uses. Change the dip halves to R.ease.inOut(p*2) and 1 − R.ease.inOut((p−0.5)*2). Consider lengthening crossfades to 0.8 s in the storyboard so a dissolve reads as a dissolve. Re-check the typography→motion overlap after this change (see that finding), because the mid-mix will now last longer.

findings.evidence: Strip 90.9–94.667 shows the wordmark settled by about 90.6 and the last tagline word complete at 92.08, then an unchanged card to 94.67. Encoded frame 94.65 confirms the final card.

Set MARK_AT 1.4→1.0, RULE_AT 2.4→1.9 and WORDS_AT 2.7→2.1, so the tagline completes at local 3.18 (91.48) and the card holds 3.2 s. If the timeline can take it, also extend scene 11 by 1.0 s in storyboard.json for a 4 s hold.

findings.problem: The crossfade into Motion lays the typography specimens over the incoming charcoal panel. 'be remembered.', 'the problem.' and 'A TALE FROM ETERNO' sit as black type on dark grey: a muddy double image of text caught mid-exit.
findings.evidence: Full-size encoded frame at 70.00: right of x 800, the Display XL and Signature specimens and the eyebrow specimen show through the half-arrived #2B2A28 panel. Strip 69.4–70.6 shows it from 69.73 to about 70.13. It will last longer once crossfades use a symmetric curve.
findings.fix: In typography.js, exit the three specimen rows, hairlines and labels (everything except the 'Typography' eyebrow) at local 5.2 over 320 ms with the exit ease, so they are gone by 5.52. The crossfade at 5.6 then brings the Motion panel over clean Linen. The Linen left column is identical in both scenes, so the dissolve reads as the panel arriving.

findings.problem: The film's emotional line, 'You can smell the ones the sea decided to give back.', is fully visible for only 3.2 s (42.70–45.90) for 11 words, about 1.5 s short. At 45.93 the dip snatches it away.
findings.evidence: Strip 39.8–41.6: the Beat B eyebrow starts at 41.10 and the words at 41.30, completing at 42.70. Strip 45.6–47.4: the line is half-washed by 46.00.
findings.fix: In one-story-per-bottle.js, bring Beat B in earlier: A_TEXT_OUT 6.1→5.7, B_IN.at 6.1→5.8, B_EYEBROW 7.3→6.7, B_WORDS 7.5→6.9 (complete at 8.3, i.e. 42.1). Beat A's Wayne line still gets 3.6 s, and the boat line gets about 3.8 s. This also stops the Wayne text exit and the photo dissolve starting on the same frame (39.9), which currently runs two motions at once.

findings.problem: The arrivals read as effects, not light. The line photos pop in: the standard 600 ms fade puts most of each photo on screen in about 3 frames. The motion scene's G7 demonstration rejects exactly this in its own comments. The 26 % soft edge laying the flat tone fields also smears Sea slate into a long dark-to-white airbrushed gradient.
findings.evidence: Strip 48.8–52.2: at 50.80 photo 1 is essentially fully present one strip frame after its fade starts, and the same happens at 50.90 for photo 2. Full-size encoded frame at 50.00: the eterno panel is a slate→Linen gradient band about 600 px wide.
findings.fix: In three-lines.js, fade the photos with R.tween(t, PHOTO_AT[i], R.dur.xl, E.inOut), matching motion.js's photo arrival, and keep the 120 ms stagger. Lay the tone fields with a narrower edge, R.softReveal(triptych, reveal, 100, 10), so the fields arrive as a clean light edge rather than a gradient.

findings.problem: The time is unbalanced between the two beats. Beat A, the whole system (ratio bar, ratio line, nine named and hexed swatches), is fully built for only 1.5 s (57.78–59.30). Beat B's grid then sits completely frozen for 3.06 s (61.04–64.10).
findings.evidence: Strip 55.3–58.0: the last chip label settles at about 57.8. Strip 58.9–61.2: the exit starts at 59.30. Frame-difference analysis shows 0.00 for all frames from 61.0 to 64.1.
findings.fix: In colour.js, overlap Beat A's build with the bar reveal. Set CHIP_AT 1.9→1.3 (chips follow the light edge across the bar) and RATIO.at 1.5→1.2, so Beat A completes at about 2.5. Move A_OUT 4.6→5.0, TITLE_B.at 5.0→5.4 and TILE_AT 5.2→5.6. Beat A then holds 2.5 s and the grid still holds 2.7 s.

findings.problem: The scene's payoff, the After-dark photo arriving out of its colour, is fully up for only about 0.4 s before the crossfade to the storefront starts. The demonstration of 'Light, not decoration.' lands and is immediately dissolved.
findings.evidence: Strip 71.0–74.9: the photo fade runs 73.60–74.80. Strip 74.8–76.0: the crossfade starts eating it at 75.13.
findings.fix: In motion.js, shift the second half earlier by 0.5 s: 'Light, not decoration.' at 2.5 (the mark has finished at 2.8, so start it at 2.9 and keep the rule-before-demonstration order by moving MARK_AT 1.6→1.3), and PHOTO.at and PUSH.at 3.9→3.4. The photo is then fully up for about 1 s before the crossfade.

findings.problem: Scene crossfades and the dip-to-linen use R.ease.standard, which starts fast. So each '0.6 s' transition is 20% done after one frame, 68% after four frames (133 ms) and 93% after nine. The dip flashes the dark amber fog to near-white Linen in about 130 ms, and the Motion panel slams dark. On screen they read as hard cuts with a flash, not the slow light the film claims to demonstrate.
findings.evidence: Per-frame means from the encoded MP4. Dip at 45.9: full-frame luma 104.6 at 45.900, then 131.8, 158.1, 180.3, 197.5 at 45.933–46.033 (27 levels per frame). Crossfade at 69.7: the right-panel region goes 240.9 → 200.3 → 161.4 → 126.6 → 103.7 over frames 2091–2095. The largest single-frame diffs in the film all sit on the first frames of these transitions: 30.3 at 45.9, 25.0 at 69.7, 21.9 at 54.7, 21.4 at 75.1. Matches the curve: standard(1/18) = 0.20, standard(4/18) = 0.68.
findings.fix: In runtime.js applyIn(), use R.ease.inOut (or a sine in-out) instead of R.ease.standard for the crossfade opacity and for both halves of the dip-to-linen/dip-to-night overlay; keep the durations. Then re-check strips at 45.8–47.2, 69.6–70.4 and 75.0–75.8: the per-frame luma step should stay under about 8 levels.

findings.problem: During the 01→02 light-wipe, scene 01's full-size bottle and the small browser bottle overlap inside the soft edge. For about five frames there are two translucent grey bottles side by side, a double exposure that reads as a compositing error at the moment the film claims 'already applied'.
findings.evidence: Encoded frames 7.633–7.767, full size at 7.733: a large ghosted eterno/wayne bottle at x ≈1230–1490 overlaps the small browser bottle at x ≈1450–1610. Both labels are legible and the browser top bar is cut by the edge. Visible in the 7.0–8.3 strip (f230, f232).
findings.fix: In scene 02, do not show the browser (frame and film together) until the wipe has cleared the big bottle. The soft edge passes x 1492 at t ≈0.86 s. Hold the browser at opacity 0 until 0.9 s, then rise it 16 px and fade it in over 0.6 s (emphasized). Keep τ = 7.0 + t so the water still continues, and push the eyebrow/sentence timings later if needed. Verify with a strip at 7.4–8.2: only one bottle may be visible in any frame.

findings.problem: In the 'applied' proof shot, the site's hero headline 'Some things are never meant to fade.' runs straight across the bottle and covers its 'wayne' label for about 4 s. The film's own rule, kept everywhere else, is that no text ever crosses the bottle. The client will see type slicing through their product on the one frame meant to prove the site is finished.
findings.evidence: Full-size frame from the MP4 at 12.5: the headline occupies y ≈632–690 across x 857–1775. The bottle sits at x ≈1450–1610, y ≈475–712, and 'meant' covers the label. Visible from the capture fade-in (≈10.6 s) to the crossfade at 14.4. The storyboard notes admit it is 'flagged to the site team'.
findings.fix: Fix the site hero's film framing (object-position to bottom) and re-capture. The equivalent in the film: in scene 02, set the film rect y from −25 to −116 (bottom-aligned; the 625-tall film has 91 px of slack under the 509 viewport). The bottle then spans y ≈384–621, clearing the headline ascenders at ≈632 and the header at ≈340. Check a full-size still at t = 5.5 (12.5 global).

findings.problem: During the 03→04 light-wipe, the hard edge between scene 03's Linen column and its Wayne panel (x = 800) shows through the soft band. For about four frames a hard vertical line runs through the incoming lamp and table: washed-out bright on the left, dark on the right.
findings.evidence: MP4 frames 34.300–34.433, full size at 34.367: a sharp luminance edge at x = 800 cuts the pendant lamp (x 740–935) and the table in half. The left half is blended with Linen, the right half with #2B2A28.
findings.fix: In scene 04, let the wipe carry only the flat Wayne world at first, and bring the tale-wayne photo in from its colour afterwards. Keep the photo at opacity 0 until t = 0.75 s (the edge clears x 1090 at about 0.72 s), then fade it 0→1 over 0.6 s, standard (the site's G7). Keep the push start at 0 so the motion is unchanged. Re-strip 33.8–35.3.

findings.problem: The 26 % soft edge of the light-wipe (about 500 px) is wide enough that busy outgoing and incoming content overlap as a double exposure. In the 10→11 wipe, translucent phone outlines and page text float over and around the returning hero bottle for about seven frames.
findings.evidence: MP4 frames 88.967–89.167, full size at 89.0: phone A's ghost bezel, 'Composed to be remembered.' paragraph and lab photo lie across the bottle at x 1222–1492. Phone B's outline frames the bottle in f2673–2675.
findings.fix: Let a transition set its own soft width: add an optional soft value to the timeline's in: {type:'light-wipe', soft}, passed to R.softReveal in applyIn. Use about 12 % for 10→11 (and consider it for 01→02). Re-strip 88.3–89.6.

findings.problem: x264 flattens the low-contrast fog and dark water into blotchy patches that crawl under the slow push. Beat B's amber fog has no grain by design, and it posterises into mottled islands that are not in the source. The dark water in scenes 01 and 11 shows the same mottling.
findings.evidence: MP4 at 44.0: contrast-stretching the fog (x 0–1000, y 0–500) shows large blotches, while the same region of tale-shadow-of-the-sea.jpg is smooth and finely textured. Faint mottling is visible unstretched at 2× (x 1300–1900, y 0–350). The dark water at 4.6 s (x 0–600, y 700–1000) shows the same patches.
findings.fix: In tools/render.mjs, add -x264-params aq-mode=3:aq-strength=1.0:deblock=-1,-1 and lower the full-render CRF to 12–13. Keep yuv420p 8-bit for player compatibility. Alternatively, keep scene 04's beat B grain at 0.01 instead of 0 (it stays invisible on the fog but dithers it). Compare stretched crops at 44.0 before and after.

findings.problem: The soft-reveal gradients over flat, close-valued tone fields break into visible diagonal striations, 8-bit steps that the encode then emphasises. They crawl as the edge crosses the triptych.
findings.evidence: MP4 at 49.9 (the triptych reveal): thin diagonal streaks every 10–20 px across the Blush clay → Linen gradient in panel 1 (values 226→236) and the Sea slate → Linen gradient in panel 2. Faintly present in the browser-painted still review/preview/film-49.90s.jpg, stronger after encoding.
findings.fix: In lib.js R.softReveal, use an eased multi-stop mask (e.g. five stops following smoothstep instead of a single linear ramp) to spread the steps. Also, while a reveal runs over flat fields, run the runtime grain at 0.008–0.01 (in scene 05, grain: t => t > 3.5 && t < 4.8 ? 0.01 : 0) to dither the banding. Re-check a still at 49.9.

findings.problem: 'Enzo 1898' on its colour-world tile is set in Cormorant's default old-style figures. The '1' becomes a small-cap 'I', so the name reads 'Enzo I898' at a glance.
findings.evidence: MP4 full size at 62.0, tile at (801.6, 636): the numerals in 'Enzo 1898' are old-style, with the 1 at x-height and the 9 descending.
findings.fix: In scenes/colour.js, set font-variant-numeric: lining-nums on the tile name blocks (or on all Cormorant names in the scene). Check the full-size still at 62.0.

findings.problem: Phone A holds the house paragraph '— tested on skin for lasting power, bottled in Cairo…' legibly for 7 s. The storyboard excluded the house page because its wear-test method is still a placeholder and the claim is unconfirmed. The same unconfirmed claim now reaches the owner through phone A.
findings.evidence: MP4 full size at 83.9 and 88.2: phone A at x 920–1295 shows the whole paragraph at about 15 px cap height. The text comes from components/home/Sections.tsx:358. The storyboard note on scene 10 says to confirm it before the meeting.
findings.fix: Get the owner's written OK on the paragraph before the meeting. Otherwise, move phone A's static scroll off the house band to a section with no claim or price (e.g. the mobile tale band 'The sea signs the ones it gives back.', css 4447–5617). Check the full 844-row window for prices or brackets before re-rendering.

findings.problem: The MP4 is tagged with the BT.709 transfer curve, but its pixels are sRGB browser paint. QuickTime and Keynote on macOS apply the BT.709 display gamma to such files, which makes them look lifted and washed out next to Chrome and VLC. Night #171614 and the Linen fields could shift on the meeting machine even though the decoded values are correct.
findings.evidence: ffprobe: color_primaries/color_space = bt709, color_transfer = bt709, range tv. tools/render.mjs passes -color_trc bt709 for frames captured from Chrome (sRGB).
findings.fix: In tools/render.mjs, tag the transfer as sRGB (-color_trc iec61966-2-1) and keep the bt709 matrix and primaries. Then, before the meeting, play the MP4 in the exact presentation app on the presentation Mac and compare the Night field at 0.5 s and the Linen field at 12.5 s against the browser stills.

findings.problem: This scene is the proof that the direction is already built, and the live homepage headline 'Some things are never meant to fade.' runs straight across my bottle. 'meant to fade.' is printed over the eterno/wayne label. Scene 01 has just shown that type never crosses the bottle, so I would stop the meeting and point at it.
findings.evidence: Encoded frame eternal-direction-draft1-11.50s.jpg. The site headline spans stage x≈855–1775 at y≈630–690, and the bottle stands at x≈1450–1610, y≈475–710. The words 'meant to' sit on the label. It is on screen from about 10.3 s (capture fade-in) to 15.0 s (end of the crossfade into 03).
findings.fix: Fix the site hero before the meeting. Constrain the hero h1 to the 5-column text area (max-width ≈ 620 css px at 1440) so it wraps as 'Some things are / never meant to fade.' left of the bottle. Then re-run reel/tools/capture-hero-clear.mjs to regenerate site/home-desktop-hero-clear.webp and re-check a full-size still at 11.5 s: no glyph may touch the bottle.

findings.problem: The small print on my bottle's label is gibberish. The line under 'wayne' should read EAU DE PARFUM and it does not. The end card holds on this bottle for the whole conversation. If I lean in and see a label that is not mine, I start asking whether this bottle is even real.
findings.evidence: Crop of reel/assets/film/001.jpg (x 1260–1470, y 560–720), which matches frames 5.50 s and 94.50 s: under 'wayne' the line reads 'EALLE BASELM' and the volume line is smeared ('59 ML / 1.9 FL OZ'). The bottle is on screen 2.8–8.2 s, inside the browser 7–15 s, and 89.3–94.7 s, and the end card is left up after the film.
findings.fix: Camera and bottle are locked, so build one clean label plate for the small print: 'EAU DE PARFUM' and '55 ML / 1.9 FL OZ', in the label's sans, matched to the label's curvature and light. Composite it on all 133 frames in reel/assets/film and on reel/assets/img/home-hero.jpg, and do the same on public/videos/home-hero.* so the site matches. Then re-render scenes 01, 02 and 11.

findings.problem: My customers are in Cairo, and there is not one Arabic character in 95 seconds. The direction includes an Arabic pairing, but the type scene shows only Latin. Apart from the word 'Cairo', nothing tells me this is an Egyptian house. The imagery reads as Italy or Greece.
findings.evidence: Frame 68.00s: the type scene shows only Cormorant Garamond and Instrument Sans. The board's Arabic pairing (Amiri 700 / IBM Plex Sans Arabic) never appears, and reel/fonts contains no Arabic face. The pictures are an olive-garden arch (53.5 s), Mediterranean sea walls (53.5 s) and a Lake Como grand tourer (phone B, 85.0 s). The only Cairo signals are the word in scene 02 and 'bottled in Cairo' at about 16 px inside phone A (85.0 s).
findings.fix: Add Amiri and IBM Plex Sans Arabic woff2 files (Google Fonts, OFL) to reel/fonts/fonts.css. Add a fourth row to scene 07 below the UI row, between y 870 and 960: a label 'Arabic · Amiri 700 / IBM Plex Sans Arabic', a right-to-left Amiri line at about 48 px, and one Plex Sans Arabic UI line. Extend the scene by about 1.5 s. Send the two Arabic lines to the owner for approval before the meeting. If they are not approved, caption the row 'Arabic copy to be written by a native copywriter' so nothing unreviewed is shown as final.

findings.problem: You tell me the direction was chosen for conversion, but I never see a product page, a price or an Add to bag in the whole film. The storefront section shows tales and moods only. As the owner of a shop, my first question will be 'where do people buy?' I also see only one of my bottles in 95 seconds.
findings.evidence: The storefront part of the film (75.1–89.5 s: frames 78.00s, 80.80s, 85.00s) shows the tales page, the mood tiles, the house band and tale cards. There is no price or product anywhere in the film. reel/assets/site/pdp-desktop.jpg exists and is clean at the top: breadcrumb, 'Wayne', the signature line, an EGP price, Fresh/Woody chips, 'Add to bag', 'Cash on delivery', and a gallery filled with Wayne's colour world.
findings.fix: Add a third window (W3) to scene 09 using the same crossfade inside the viewport: R.capture(viewport, 'pdp-desktop', 1440).scroll(36), showing css 36–776, with the left-column label 'Wayne'. Hold it for about 2.5 s. Extend the scene or trim W1's hold (76.2–78.5 s). The empty gallery reads as Wayne's colour world (the rule the film has just shown at 73.6 s), and 'Cash on delivery' plus the EGP price are the most Cairo things on the site. Confirm the price (EGP 1,560) with the owner beforehand.

findings.problem: The film's emotional peak is my best-selling scent and the one tale written in full, and the film never names it. The Wayne tale gets its name, but the boat tale says only 'A tale from eterno'. The tales page later shows it only by its title. So I cannot connect this moment to the bottle I sell.
findings.evidence: Frame 43.50s: the eyebrow reads 'A TALE FROM ETERNO'. Frame 36.50s (beat A) reads 'A TALE FROM ETERNO · WAYNE'. Frame 78.00s: the site shows 'A TALE FROM ETERNO · 3 MIN READ' and 'The sea signs the ones it gives back.' 'Shadow of the Sea' appears only as a small tile label at 60–64 s.
findings.fix: Change the beat B eyebrow to 'A tale from eterno · Shadow of the Sea' at (120, 772), with the same spec (Instrument Sans 600, 18 px, caps, 0.14em, Dune). It is about 520 px wide and stays clear of the boat and the signature line.

findings.problem: The film opens on a symbol I have never seen, a circle with a bar next to an infinity sign, and brings it back three times. Nobody ever tells me what it is. At first glance it reads as 'G∞', and it is not the looped mark printed above 'eterno' on my bottle. I will assume you have changed my logo without asking.
findings.evidence: Frame 1.60s shows the mark drawn alone at centre as the film's opening. At 30–40 s (frames 31.50s, 36.50s) it is the watermark. At 71.3–72.5 s (frame 73.50s) it draws again. The bottle label at 5.50s and 94.50s carries a different small looped mark. No caption anywhere names it.
findings.fix: In scene 08, once the mark has finished drawing (local 2.8 s), rise a caption centred under it in the panel at y ≈ 640. Use the eyebrow 'The e∞ mark' with the board line 'Loader, favicon, cart empty state, section ornament.' underneath (Instrument Sans 18 px, Dune). Move 'Light, not decoration.' and the photo fade 0.6 s later and extend the scene by 0.6 s, so the rule 'one thing at a time' still holds.

findings.problem: The end card sets my name 'eternal' in a book serif right beside my bottle, whose label carries our calligraphic looped logotype. Nothing in the film explains the relationship, so the last frame, left up for the whole discussion, invites 'which one is our logo?'
findings.evidence: Frame 94.50s: 'eternal' is set in Cormorant Garamond 600 at 168 px (x 120–605) while the bottle label at x≈1300–1440 shows the script 'eterno' logotype. They are side by side from 89.7 to 94.7 s. The board's own rationale ('The serif echoes the soft, calligraphic wordmark on the bottle') never appears in the film.
findings.fix: In scene 07, add a short wordmark row or beat. Set the site wordmark 'eternal' (Cormorant 600, 0.02em) next to a framed crop of the bottle's 'eterno' logotype, taken from reel/assets/img/home-hero.jpg, region x≈1290–1450, y≈540–615, scaled up about 2x. Caption it with the board line 'The serif echoes the soft, calligraphic wordmark on the bottle.' The end card then reads as a deliberate echo rather than a replacement.

findings.problem: After three beautiful photographs, principle 04 gives me a flat charcoal box with a small orange square in the corner. I cannot tell that this is Wayne's colour world, and the orange square looks like a missing image or a leftover UI element. It is the weakest frame in the film and sits right before the emotional core.
findings.evidence: Frame 31.50s: the right panel (x 800–1920) is flat #2B2A28, with a 56 px Golden hour square at (1744, 120) and a faint cropped mark. It holds still from 30.8 to 33.8 s after the reveal from 29.3 s. The square carries on through 04 beat A (36.50s). What it means (a world's second colour) is explained only at 60–64 s.
findings.fix: Label the world where the square is. Rise a caption 'eterno · Wayne — colour world' (Instrument Sans 600, 18 px, caps, Dune) right-aligned to x 1720 at y 138, level with the chip, as P4's text rises. Keep it identical in scene 04 beat A so it holds through the wipe. Also consider starting scene 04's wipe about 1 s earlier so the empty hold is under 2 s.

findings.problem: The large watermark of the mark is cut off at the right edge of the frame, so the infinity loses its right loop and the mark reads as 'e α'.
findings.evidence: Frames 31.50s and 36.50s: the 1000 px watermark (strokes x 1142–1920+) is clipped at x 1920. The right half of the ∞ is missing, leaving an alpha shape.
findings.fix: Scale the watermark down so it sits whole inside the frame, e.g. R.mark({x: 1120, y: 640, width: 720, stroke 2.8, opacity 0.07}): strokes at about x 1150–1817, y 715–925. It stays clear of the Wayne photo (ends x 1090) and the text column (ends y 614). Apply identically in 03 P4 and 04 beat A.

findings.problem: The light-wipe into the dark Wayne scene reads as a white flash, not as low warm light. The previous slide's headline also shows through the photo for a moment.
findings.evidence: Strip 33.8–35.0 s and frame 34.30s: the wipe's leading edge is a near-white band sweeping across the dark room (34.2–34.5 s). The P4 text ('…tory / …tle / colour world') is double-exposed over the chair and table. The same band on the Linen scenes (7.0 s) reads fine.
findings.fix: In the runtime light-wipe, pick the band colour from the incoming scene. On dark scenes, draw the highlight in Golden hour #B97A2B at ≤ 25 % with soft-light blending instead of near-white. Narrow the soft zone for dark destinations (e.g. 26 → 14 %) so outgoing type is never seen over the incoming photo for more than 2–3 frames.

findings.problem: As my bottle returns for the ending, a half-transparent phone sits on top of it. The car and the Forbidden Apple card show through the bottle for a moment, which muddies the bookend.
findings.evidence: Strip 88.5–89.6 s and frame 89.10s: phone B (x 1425–1800) is still about 50 % visible over the bottle (x 1222–1492) from 89.0 to 89.2 s. At 89.0 s phone A's edge also crosses the bottle.
findings.fix: Bookend scene 01's reveal. Let the runtime wipe uncover Night, and keep scene 11's film layer masked until about 0.9 s. Then reveal the film with its own R.softReveal(film, R.tween(t, 0.9, 1.0, R.ease.inOut), 100, 26). Delay the scrim and text by the same 0.3 s so no phone is ever seen over the bottle.

findings.problem: 'Mobile is the primary device.' sounds like a note to the developers. It is the only headline in the film that talks about hardware rather than my house or my customer, and it flattens the mood just before the ending.
findings.evidence: Frame 85.00s: the headline sits beside the two phones from 83.0 to 89.5 s. Every other headline is either brand copy ('Composed to be remembered.') or a principle ('One thing at a time.').
findings.fix: Keep the eyebrow 'The storefront' and change the headline to the customer's side of the same rule, e.g. two lines 'Designed for the / phone first.' (Cormorant 600, 64 px, same positions (120, 300)/(120, 367)). Keep the word-by-word rise.

results.problem: The site H1 'Some things are never meant to fade.' runs across the Wayne bottle and its label from about 10.3 s to 15.0 s. Reported by brand-type (major, 12.5), finishing-qa (major, 12.5) and client-eye (blocker, 11.5); treated as one issue.
results.detail: Verified first. In the encoded frame at 12.50 s, 'meant to' sits on the 'wayne' part of the label. From the alpha channel of the capture, the headline ink runs from css 503 (ascender top) to 597 (descender), which is stage y 632–698. From film frame 001, the bottle spans film px x 1222–1493 and y 332–738, which is stage y 475–710 at the old offset. Fix, in reel/scenes/already-applied.js only: both blended film images are now bottom-aligned in the viewport, FILM.y = VIEW_H − 900·S = −116 (was −25). x, w and h are unchanged and the page capture is not moved, masked or scrolled. The bottle now stands at stage y 384–619. That is below the header (nav ≈ 332) and above the headline's tallest ascender (632). The 625 px film still covers the 509 px viewport, so no image edge shows. I chose the full −116 over brand-type's −105 because −105 leaves only about 2 px between the glass base and the ascenders. Checked in full-size solo stills at local 3.6, 5.5 and 7.97 (global 10.6, 12.5 and 14.97) and in an enlarged crop of the bottle at 5.5. No glyph touches the bottle; the headline sits on the stone under it with the bottle's reflection behind 'meant'. Trade-off: the thin band of sky above the horizon is now above the viewport, so the top of the window shows the warm haze over the sea instead. The water still runs at τ = 7.0 + t.

results.problem: Double image of the bottle during the 01→02 light-wipe (about 7.62–7.85 s). Scene 01's full-frame bottle and the small bottle in the browser overlap in the soft 26 % edge. Reported by motion-pacing (major, 7.72) and finishing-qa (major, 7.70); treated as one issue.
results.detail: Verified in the encoded frame at 7.72 s: two translucent bottles at two scales, both labels legible.
